7 product updates shipped in October 2026. See [Product Updates](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog) for the latest.

October 27, 2026

No SDK Update Required

## Find sensitive data leaking from your app with Sensitive Data Findings[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#find-sensitive-data-leaking-from-your-app-with-sensitive-data-findings)

![The Sensitive data findings page in app settings, showing a table of findings with their severity, reports, and app versions.](https://docs.luciq.ai/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1627791424-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FX5AT2gAek6Hb4IQeMXHI%252Fuploads%252Fgit-blob-183381216414b8707749460d796684d3f54d7707%252Fsensitive-data-findings-list.jpg%3Falt%3Dmedia&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=ffb00e835cd2b8aad50f328bf5056d16&sv=3)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary)

See API keys, tokens, and credentials that your app leaks in console and network logs reported to Luciq, and ignore the ones you've confirmed are safe.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new)

- A new **Sensitive data findings** page under **Settings** \> **App settings** \> **Data privacy** lists sensitive data that leaked from your app and was reported to Luciq.

- It currently covers Crash Reporting, and detects leaks in console logs and network logs.

- Each finding shows its severity, the number of crash reports and app versions it appears in, and when it was first and last seen.

- Open a finding to see sample reports with the value redacted, plus advice on what your engineer needs to do.

- Jump from a report to the log entry that contains the value, highlighted in the crash occurrence's logs.

- Ignore a finding you've reviewed, and reopen it later from the **Ignored** tab.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters)

- You can find secrets your app writes to logs or sends in network requests, without opening reports one by one.

- You can see how widespread a leak is and which log it comes from, so it's clear what to fix first.


#### Availability[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#availability)

- Available per app token.


[Documentation](https://docs.luciq.ai/product-guides-and-integrations/product-guides/luciq-pii-masking/sensitive-data-findings)

October 27, 2026

No SDK Update Required

## Find the code behind slow launches, screens, and requests with APM Optimizations[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#find-the-code-behind-slow-launches-screens-and-requests-with-apm-optimizations)

![The Optimizations section of the Debugging tab, showing a list of issues and investigations and the details of the selected issue.](https://docs.luciq.ai/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1627791424-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FX5AT2gAek6Hb4IQeMXHI%252Fuploads%252Fgit-blob-441319fca19feb7336929705418d59081e0aad44%252Fapm-optimizations-issues-list.jpg%3Falt%3Dmedia&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=0e18b9cb205581ad3a6aa2a625e8808f&sv=3)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-1)

Paste one prompt per APM metric into your coding agent, and it reads your repo and sends every code issue behind a slow launch, screen, or request to Luciq.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-1)

- Each supported APM metric now has a **Debugging** tab with its own prompt, tailored to what that metric measures.

- Copy the prompt into your coding agent, connected to the Luciq MCP and your app's repository. The agent checks your APM data for a real bottleneck and traces it to the code responsible.

- The agent sends the full list of issues in your code back to Luciq automatically, each with its investigation, root cause, and recommended actions. They appear in the **Optimizations** section of the tab.

- Your code stays on your machine.

- Ask your coding agent to make the prompt a routine, so it re-runs on its own.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-1)

- You can see which launch phase, screen, or request is slow. Now you can also see what in your code causes it, without a blind fix or opening occurrences one by one to find the pattern.

- One prompt gets you the full list of issues for a metric.


[Documentation](https://docs.luciq.ai/product-guides-and-integrations/product-guides/application-performance-monitoring/apm-optimizations)

SDK Update Required

## iOS crashes now show the termination reason behind a SIGABRT[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#ios-crashes-now-show-the-termination-reason-behind-a-sigabrt)

![A crash on the dashboard with the exception SIGABRT at -[CheckoutSession dealloc] and the message Cannot form weak reference to instance (0x114004aa0) of class CheckoutSession. It is possible that this object was over-released, or is in the process of deallocation.](https://docs.luciq.ai/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1627791424-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FX5AT2gAek6Hb4IQeMXHI%252Fuploads%252Fgit-blob-19af3f2184532eec5ee09d6f4d6da39c9c847280%252Fsigabrt-termination-reason.png%3Falt%3Dmedia&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=3cf20d176ce5431cc29209809d56a93f&sv=3)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-2)

The crash message now shows why a system framework like the Objective-C runtime stopped your app, which makes debugging much easier.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-2)

- Crashes that a system framework ends with a termination reason now show that reason as the crash message, such as `Cannot form weak reference to instance (0x…) of class CheckoutSession. It is possible that this object was over-released, or is in the process of deallocation.`

- This works for any system framework that stops your app with a termination reason. To name a few: the Objective-C runtime, UIKit, Core Animation, Metal, and XPC.

- The SDK captures the reason when the crash happens. The message shows on the crash list and on the crash details page.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-2)

- SIGABRT crashes raised by system frameworks are now far easier to debug.

- Crashes that are no longer reported as an exception but as a SIGABRT in apps built with the iOS 27 SDK, such as collection view assertions, still show their crash message, so they stay easy to debug.


#### Availability[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#availability-1)

- Available from iOS SDK 19.12.0.

No SDK Update Required

## Filter Session Replay by email, just like Bugs[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#filter-session-replay-by-email-just-like-bugs)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-3)

Find sessions by the user's email with the same four operators you already use on Bugs: Equals, Doesn't equal, Contains, and Doesn't contain.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-3)

- A new **Email** filter in the Session Replay filter bar, right after **App version**, on both the sessions list and the session details page.

- Four operators: **Equals**, **Doesn't equal**, **Contains**, and **Doesn't contain**.

- Matching ignores case, so `Jane.Doe@Example.com` also matches `jane.doe@example.com`.

- **Contains** matches any part of the address, such as a whole domain like `@example.com`.

- **Doesn't equal** and **Doesn't contain** also include sessions that have no email.

- Works together with the **Search by User ID, Email** box and every other filter, and stays applied when you move between sessions or share the link.

- Text filters on Bugs and crash occurrences now apply as soon as you press Enter, and keep the operator you picked.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-3)

- Pull up every session from one company or domain in a single search.

- Leave internal and test accounts out of the list with **Doesn't contain**.


#### Availability[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#availability-2)

- Available wherever you have Session Replay. Emails come from the user identification API in your app.


[Documentation](https://docs.luciq.ai/product-guides-and-integrations/product-guides/session-replay#user-identification)

## Add your own network masking keys from the dashboard[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#add-your-own-network-masking-keys-from-the-dashboard)

![The Network masking keys page under Data privacy in the app settings, listing a Session-Token header key and a payment_address query param key](https://docs.luciq.ai/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1627791424-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FX5AT2gAek6Hb4IQeMXHI%252Fuploads%252Fgit-blob-7d22167fe463bb8ce3d72529997858fc2567a706%252Fnetwork-masking-keys-page.png%3Falt%3Dmedia&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=82081275db2a77b1d354b185523bff35&sv=3)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-4)

Pick which extra headers and query parameters the SDK masks in network logs, straight from your app settings. No more waiting on a support request.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-4)

- A new **Data privacy → Network masking keys** page in your app settings, where you can add, rename, and delete your own masking keys.

- Each key is a header or a query parameter name. The SDK replaces its value with an asterisk (\*) on the device, so the value never reaches Luciq's servers.

- Matching ignores case, so `X-Session-Id` also masks `x-session-id`.

- The page also lists the default keys the SDK always masks, such as `Authorization`, `token`, and `password`. They stay on and can't be edited or removed.

- Keys you asked support to add before are already on the page, ready to edit.

- Changes apply from the next session. You don't need to release a new app version.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-4)

- You control which of your app's own headers and query parameters stay private, without opening a support request.

- Sensitive values are masked before they leave the device, so they never show up in your network logs.


#### Availability[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#availability-3)

- Available for apps with automatic network masking turned on, which is the default from SDK 14.2.0.

- Adding, editing, and deleting keys needs permission to manage app settings.


[Documentation](https://docs.luciq.ai/product-guides-and-integrations/product-guides/luciq-pii-masking/network-log-masking#adding-your-own-masking-keys)

## iOS crashes now show the Swift runtime failure that caused them[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#ios-crashes-now-show-the-swift-runtime-failure-that-caused-them)

![A crash on the dashboard with the exception SIGTRAP at SwiftCrashDemo.crash() and the message Swift runtime failure: Unexpectedly found nil while unwrapping an Optional value](https://docs.luciq.ai/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F1627791424-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FX5AT2gAek6Hb4IQeMXHI%252Fuploads%252Fgit-blob-0031211f4e4308cd6dece5804531765eeddf5895%252Fswift_runtime_failure.png%3Falt%3Dmedia&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=a7869976390bae282c6985aefa21f1e2&sv=3)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-5)

The crash message now shows the reason behind any Swift runtime failure, which makes debugging much easier.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-5)

- Crashes caused by a Swift runtime failure now show the reason as the crash message, such as `Swift runtime failure: Unexpectedly found nil while unwrapping an Optional value`.

- This works for any Swift runtime failure. To name a few: force unwrapping a `nil` optional, an out-of-range array index, and arithmetic overflow.

- Luciq reads the reason from your app's dSYM when it symbolicates the crash. The message shows on the crash list and on the crash details page.

- Crash grouping doesn't change. Only the message is updated, so existing crash groups keep their occurrences and history.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-5)

- Swift crashes are now far easier to debug.


#### Availability[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#availability-4)

- Live for all iOS apps.


[Documentation](https://docs.luciq.ai/ios/setup-luciq-for-ios/setup-crash-reporting/symbolication#swift-runtime-failure-messages)

October 1, 2026

No SDK Update Required

## Health Status, Period Summary, and Release Markers on APM Details Pages[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#health-status-period-summary-and-release-markers-on-apm-details-pages)

#### Summary[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#summary-6)

APM details pages now open with a day-by-day health status, a period summary, and release markers on the charts. A bad day and the version next to it stand out at a glance.

#### What's new?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#whats-new-6)

- **Health status:** every APM metric details page now opens with one cell per day, colored by that day's Apdex rating, so a bad day stands out at a glance.

- **Summary row:** Apdex, throughput, unique users, and other metrics for the selected period, each with its change compared to the previous period.

- **Release markers:** every app release appears on the Apdex, throughput, and latency charts. Hover over a marker to see the version and release date.


#### Why this matters?[Direct link to heading](https://docs.luciq.ai/changelog/readme/2026-10\#why-this-matters-6)

- You can tell whether a metric is healthy before reading a single chart, and see quickly when it isn't.

- When there's a dip, the release marker next to it points to the version to investigate.
